correctness.rationale: Direct path-basis multiplication produces the three displayed homogeneous equations for centralizing a fixed element. The case analysis is exhaustive: pairwise-distinct diagonals; each of three two-equal diagonal patterns; all equal with zero/one/two nonzero first-layer arrow coordinates. The tensor map (x′,y′) ↦ x⊗y′−x′⊗y has one-dimensional kernel for x,y both nonzero. Each table count follows from coordinate cardinalities, including membership tests in x⊗W and V⊗y. Counts sum to q^(3+r+s+rs). Nine complete small-domain finite-field enumerations, including F4 and (2,2,2), reproduce each centralizer-dimension histogram; the arbitrary-parameter proof is symbolic. The formula does not purport to classify the actual centralizer subalgebras.

value.rationale: Finite-ring commuting probability is a motivated invariant, and its complete centralizer-dimension distribution is stronger. The nontrivial radical-square layer V⊗W creates a new tensor-membership stratification absent from Kronecker and radical-square-zero algebras. The theorem gives a complete two-parameter natural family and distinguishes same-field equal-dimension algebras A_(2,7) and A_(3,5) by their exact commuting probability. This is not an arbitrary small numerical increment, an elementary one-arrow substitution or a single unmotivated slice.
